fixes.explanation: Paul says they've given themselves over “…with a craving for more.” That craving never says "okay, that's enough." It just asks again. I think this part is heavy.
Paul doesn't say that here. What he names is “…a craving for more.” That's what they have, friend.
Paul says it plainly: “But this is not the way you came to know Christ.” He's setting the believers' road next to the Gentiles' road, and they don't match. So the statement is true.
Paul doesn't mention Greek wisdom here. He says they were taught “…in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus…” The measuring stick is Jesus, not a famous thinker.
Paul says to put off “…your former way of life, your old self…” Two names for one thing, and both get taken off. That's step one in his three steps.
I see why "younger days" sounds right, since "former" is in the verse. But Paul isn't talking about age. He calls it “…your old self…”
Abraham, whom God called out of his homeland (Genesis 12:1), isn't who Paul names here. He says the new self is created to be like God. That's the pattern, and it's much taller than any one person.
That's not Paul's reason in this verse. He says to speak truthfully “…for we are all members of one another.” The reason is how closely we're joined together.

Paul says, “…but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.” Words are meant to build. That's a high bar for the mouth. I'm still working on it myself.

This one does come right out of the verse. Paul says the believers were sealed in the Holy Spirit of God “…for the day of redemption.” So the statement is true. He also says, “And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God…”
